units.translation: V. 401 ⟦1⟧ properly with the stem, ⟦2⟧ (Hesych.), cf. ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧. 1056. In the literal sense of trees Sophocles ⟦5⟧.

⟦1⟧ 402 belongs in sense actually to the preceding, of the spoil selected for Athena (cf. ⟦2⟧), yet moving the comma after ⟦3⟧ would make what follows too bare. Theseus' sons Demophon and Acamas appear only in the later epic, where they find their grandmother Aethra in conquered Troy, see Proclus' excerpt from Arctinus' ⟦4⟧; but this justification of the Athenian claim to Sigeum certainly goes back to the time of Peisistratus. In Euripides' Heraclidae the sons of Theseus are the princes of the land; but in the Eumenides nothing further occurs of them, and according to Aeschylus the Athenian democracy appears as already founded by Theseus, cf. especially Athena's speech to the people 681 ff. — On the dative with ⟦5⟧ cf. Kühner-Gerth I, 426 f.

⟦1⟧: recalls ⟦2⟧ (Weckl.). ‘⟦3⟧ occurs only here (for Homer ⟦4⟧ 106 is ⟦5⟧ the correct spelling), but ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧ makes the sense “noisy movement” unambiguous (cf. also Ar. ⟦8⟧. 407); thus = ⟦9⟧ (below 424). Since the aegis appears on monuments and vases of the 6th century as laid around like a collar or mantle (see Preller-Robert Myth. 191), it was easy to make of the mantle a kind of billowing sail (Schol.). On ⟦10⟧. see above.

With ⟦1⟧ one could be satisfied (cf. Paley), but ⟦2⟧ (M) demands the correction to ⟦3⟧, a very easy one according to the script of the Aristotle papyrus, where the H shortened at the bottom left and the Y are confusingly similar.
409 ⟦1⟧ with accusative also Frg. 158 (elsewhere with dative, as ⟦2⟧); likewise ⟦3⟧ 446, ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧, Kühner-Gerth Synt. I, 313 f.
410 Transition to the accusative, which is equally possible with ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧); the dative would have become awkward at 412.
410 ⟦1⟧ generally begotten, including gods and men.
⟦1⟧ as ⟦2⟧ Ag. 359. 474. After ⟦3⟧ the following verse is corrupted by unconscious assimilation; for the correctness of the correction ⟦4⟧ (Robortellus) instead of ⟦5⟧ is not to be doubted.
